country_context.note: This profile documents English as used in the United States. It must not be treated as a description of every English-speaking country.

rhoticity, vowel shifts, stress, rhythm, and connected speech
greetings and leave-taking
directness and indirectness by context
politeness, requests, disagreement, small talk
regional, generational, and community variation
standard written American English
spelling differences from other national standards
grammar and punctuation in formal contexts
formal, academic, workplace, and public-service registers
colloquial contractions and reductions
regional and community vocabulary
youth and internet slang with dated usage labels
African American English and other community varieties described on their own terms
common profanity and taboo expressions
severity, target, and pragmatic force
reclaimed or in-group usage versus hostile use
